---
title: "Modelling diversity against covariates"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", out.width = "100%",
  dpi = 150, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4
)
```

Diversity estimates are often the response in a model of environmental
drivers. Two things matter: the estimates should be comparable (equal
coverage or asymptotic), and their uncertainty should carry through to
the model. tidydiversity results are tidy tibbles, so this takes a few
lines.

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(tidydiversity)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
set.seed(2026)
sites <- distinct(ant_gradient, site, transect, elevation)
```

## Model-ready estimates

`tidy()` renames columns to the broom conventions and adds an
inverse-variance `weight`; `add_site_data()` joins covariates that are
constant within each site.

```{r tidy}
est <- div_standardise(ant_gradient,
  q = c(0, 1, 2), .by = transect,
  nboot = 200
) |>
  tidy() |>
  add_site_data(sites)
est
```

## Approaches {.tabset}

### Weighted lm

Inverse-variance weights give less influence to imprecise estimates.

```{r lm}
shannon <- filter(est, q == 1)
fit_lm <- lm(estimate ~ elevation + I(elevation^2) + transect,
  data = shannon, weights = weight
)
broom::tidy(fit_lm, conf.int = TRUE)
```

### Mixed model

With repeated sites or blocks, add a random effect with **lme4** (or
**glmmTMB**, which takes the same formula).

```{r lmer, message = FALSE}
fit_mm <- lme4::lmer(estimate ~ elevation + (1 | transect),
  data = shannon, weights = weight / mean(weight)
)
summary(fit_mm)$coefficients
```

### GAM

**mgcv** fits a smooth response along the gradient.

```{r gam, fig.alt = "GAM smooth of Shannon diversity along elevation"}
fit_gam <- mgcv::gam(estimate ~ s(elevation, k = 5) + transect,
  data = shannon, weights = weight / mean(weight), method = "REML"
)
summary(fit_gam)$s.table
grid <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  elevation = seq(200, 1600, by = 20),
  transect = c("north", "south")
)
pred <- predict(fit_gam, grid, se.fit = TRUE)
grid$fit <- pred$fit
grid$se <- pred$se.fit
ggplot(grid, aes(elevation, fit, colour = transect, fill = transect)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = fit - 1.96 * se, ymax = fit + 1.96 * se),
    alpha = 0.2, colour = NA
  ) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_pointrange(aes(y = estimate, ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high),
    data = shannon
  ) +
  scale_colour_tidydiversity() +
  scale_fill_tidydiversity() +
  labs(
    x = "Elevation (m)",
    y = "Shannon diversity (effective number of species)",
    colour = NULL, fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_tidydiversity()
```

### Count model for richness

Observed richness is a count, but it depends on sampling effort. Model
standardised richness with a Gamma GLM (positive, continuous), or observed
richness with a Poisson GLM and log sample size as an offset.

```{r glm}
rich <- filter(est, q == 0)
broom::tidy(glm(estimate ~ elevation + transect,
  data = rich,
  family = Gamma(link = "log"), weights = weight / mean(weight)
))
obs <- div_hill(ant_gradient, q = 0) |> add_site_data(sites)
broom::tidy(glm(diversity ~ elevation + transect + offset(log(n)),
  data = obs, family = poisson
))
```

## Propagating uncertainty with bootstrap draws

Weights use only the standard error. `div_boot()` returns the bootstrap
replicates themselves, so the whole model can be refitted to each
replicate and the spread of the coefficients includes the estimation
uncertainty in the response.

```{r boot}
draws <- div_boot(ant_gradient,
  q = 1, type = "standardised",
  coverage = 0.9, nboot = 200
) |>
  add_site_data(sites)
draws

slopes <- draws |>
  group_by(.draw) |>
  group_modify(\(d, key) {
    broom::tidy(lm(diversity ~ elevation + transect, data = d))
  }) |>
  ungroup() |>
  filter(term == "elevation")
quantile(slopes$estimate, c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975))
```

```{r boot-plot, fig.height = 3, fig.alt = "Bootstrap distribution of the elevation slope"}
ggplot(slopes, aes(estimate * 100)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = td_palette(1)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = "Change in Shannon diversity per 100 m", y = "Bootstrap draws") +
  theme_tidydiversity()
```

## Beta diversity

### Distance decay

`beta_decay()` gives one row per pair of sites with the distance along
one or more gradients. Several columns give Euclidean distance.

```{r decay}
decay <- beta_decay(ant_gradient, elevation, .by = transect)
broom::tidy(lm(turnover ~ distance + transect, data = decay))
```

Pairs are not independent, so test the relationship with a Mantel test
rather than the lm p-values.

```{r mantel}
north <- filter(ant_gradient, transect == "north")
d_beta <- beta_dist(beta_pair(north), "turnover")
d_elev <- dist(distinct(north, site, elevation)$elevation)
vegan::mantel(d_beta, d_elev, permutations = 999)
```

### PERMANOVA and ordination

```{r permanova, message = FALSE}
bray <- beta_dist(beta_pair(ant_gradient, index = "bray"))
vegan::adonis2(bray ~ elevation + transect,
  data = sites,
  permutations = 999
)
```

```{r nmds, fig.height = 4, fig.alt = "NMDS ordination of sites coloured by elevation"}
nmds <- vegan::metaMDS(bray, trace = FALSE)
bind_cols(sites, as.data.frame(vegan::scores(nmds))) |>
  ggplot(aes(NMDS1, NMDS2, colour = elevation, shape = transect)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_colour_viridis_c() +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(colour = "Elevation (m)", shape = NULL) +
  theme_tidydiversity(legend_position = "right")
```
